method: On a disposable 'ZZ probe detail' task's detail view in each app: (a) typed one character into the title, clicked far outside the modal, then clicked Discard, recording whether the whole detail modal was still open; (b) reopened the detail, typed one character, clicked the form's own Cancel button, then Discard, recording whether the modal was still open; (c) reopened the detail, typed one character, pressed Escape to raise the confirmation, then pressed Escape again, recording document.activeElement and whether the draft survived. Cancelled the edit cleanly at the end (Cancel then Discard, no residual draft).

a_outsideClickThenDiscard.verdict: MATCH -- both apps close the WHOLE detail modal after Discard when the confirmation was triggered by an outside click. This fixes round 3's DIFFERS (meologue previously kept the modal open here). role differs (dialog vs alertdialog), meologue's own recorded choice, not counted as a difference.

b_cancelButtonThenDiscard.verdict: MATCH -- both apps keep the detail modal open after Discard when the confirmation was triggered by the form's own Cancel button; only the edit ends.

c_escapeThenEscapeAgain.verdict: MATCH -- both apps: the second Escape closes only the confirmation, the draft ('ZZ probe detailZ') survives, and focus lands back on the Task name editor (tag DIV, role textbox, aria-label 'Task name'). This fixes round 3's finding that meologue returned focus to document.body instead of the title editor.

overallVerdict.note: Both of round 3's DET-15 differences (outside-click+Discard modal scope, and Escape-in-confirmation focus target) are now fixed in meologue. All three scenarios (a/b/c) are structurally and behaviorally identical between Todoist and meologue, modulo the already-accepted role='dialog' vs role='alertdialog' naming choice.
